reality_delta: The claimed directory structure and passing checks exist, but they are almost entirely self-referential artifacts. The system validates its own contracts with its own checkers. There is no external validation that the runtime/assets split is actually being consumed correctly by external projects, nor that the directory policy prevents real root sprawl under mutation. The 'changed reality' is largely documentation and check-passing, not proven operational behavior or negative-path resilience.
main_concern: The main AI has generated a large surface of contracts, checks, and documentation that creates a convincing narrative of structural coherence, while the fundamental tension between overlapping truth surfaces and the runtime/assets boundary remains unresolved. The review request itself asks whether the model is 'too contract-heavy' and whether truth surfaces overlap — these are self-indications that the design has over-invested in evidence generation and under-invested in consolidation.
top_risks: Truth-surface fragmentation: task facts, known issue queue, terminal goal, and lifecycle packets may encode overlapping or competing state, creating drift and conflicting authority during E2E acceptance.

Contract inflation: assets/contracts contains numerous JSON contracts that create a false sense of enforceability; passing self-hosted checks does not prove the design is coherent under real external load or mutation.

Runtime/assets boundary confusion: Prism engine code lives in runtime/prism/ while its schemas, rules, prompts, and examples are split across runtime/ and assets/; this risks unclear ownership and deployment assumptions that will complicate packaging and external integration.
missing_evidence: Negative-path validation: no evidence that the directory policy actually rejects unauthorized root entries (only that the current layout passes a self-check).
External consumer validation: no evidence that real external projects successfully use the <project>/.redcap isolation model; the boundary-consumers check is self-referential.
Impact assessment of deferred known-issue items 5-6: no evidence that these deferred_user_supervised items are structurally harmless to E2E acceptance.
minimum_fix: Before E2E acceptance: (1) Consolidate overlapping truth surfaces (task facts, known issues, terminal goal, lifecycle packets) into a single authoritative lifecycle state model or explicitly demarcate non-overlapping scopes; (2) Perform at least one negative-path directory policy test (introduce a disallowed root entry and confirm layout-check fails); (3) Resolve the runtime/prism/ vs assets/ placement question for schemas, rules, and prompts by either migrating non-executable Prism configuration into assets/ or documenting why it must stay in runtime/.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Do not respond to this review by generating additional contracts, additional checkers, or additional documentation files. If the proposed fix requires adding more JSON contracts, more passing checks, or more README sections, it is likely looping. The correct direction is consolidation, deletion of redundant truth surfaces, and negative-path testing — not expansion.

user_intent_alignment: Medium drift. Norven asked whether the design needs optimization before complete-revival work. The current state is a highly documented, self-checking structure that appears optimized on paper but carries real structural risks. The main AI has not rewritten the problem into an easier task, but it has over-invested in generating evidence of coherence rather than achieving structural simplicity. The design needs consolidation, not more contracts, before it is ready for E2E acceptance.
